# nODD ECAL layouts - reviewer overview

Si-W and ALLEGRO LAr candidates. Review entry, not a TDR.

Snapshot: 2026-10-14. [Four-page PDF](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/ecal-layout-review.pdf).

## 1 - Candidate layouts

Both candidates retain the documented tracker (45,646 sensitive planes) and the proposed inner solenoid (3 T central target; [PR #64](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/64), open). Its radial service reservation reaches 1.64 m; the computed vessel ends at r=1.559 m and |z|=3.85 m. These DRAFT prototypes have no complete-detector, installed-field or engineering acceptance.

![Si-W candidate R-Z view with tracker, conditional solenoid and HCAL outline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/figures/layout001-rz.png)

LAYOUT-001: Si-W ECAL, enlarged HCAL outline and empty service/FCal reservations. FCal and muon systems remain unbuilt.

![LAr candidate R-Z view with enlarged calorimeter and service allocations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/figures/layout002-rz.png)

LAYOUT-002: LAr ECAL, enlarged HCAL outline and empty service/forward reservations. Neither forward collar nor FCal is built.

## 2 - Si-W ECAL prototype

Open component proposals: [PR #71](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/71) (Si-W ECAL barrel prototype) and [PR #70](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/70) (Si-W ECAL endcap prototype). The same sampling and board stack is carried through sixteen barrel sectors and sixteen wedge carriers per endcap. [PR #76](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/76) adds service/forward envelopes under [DES034](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/0a26796518d690bf26934d2864d63ecad7582675/docs/design/DES-034-siw-service-envelopes.md).

| Element | Current prototype choice |
| --- | --- |
| Sampling / sensors | 48 layers; 1.9 mm tungsten alloy and 0.5 mm silicon. Standard 90 mm blanks have an 88 mm active window and 5.5 mm pad pitch; physical guards remain passive. |
| Barrel construction | Seven 1 m slabs plus two short end slabs per sector/layer. Alternating ±96 mm shifts move service joints through depth; 94 mm boards on a 96 mm pitch retain real gaps. |
| Endcap packing | 76 squares plus 36 custom edge sensors per wedge/layer; 29 mask profiles. The 100 mm aperture apothem, 30 mm inner support and 120 mm outer service bay are unsigned allocations. |
| Support / cooling | Aluminium skins and frames, explicit PCB/ASIC/thermal contacts; a 3 mm copper plate with 2 mm-OD Ti/water runs. External collectors/ports remain absent; PR76 reserves an outer backbone and HCAL rear egress. |

### Material and service drivers

Recorded model masses are 299.003 t for the barrel and 98.949 t for both endcaps. Copper contributes 119.693/40.591 t, dominated by the cooling plates. Continuous heat hypotheses give 188.40/71.05 kW; the summed ideal water flow is 12.414 kg/s for a 5 K rise. These are inventory/power calculations, not thermal or hydraulic qualification. A 300 mm annulus and 400 mm rear break reserve cable/water exits; local cassette ports and support loads remain open. The 30 mm front seam is installation-only; services are allocated outside the endcap.

### Coverage and evidence limits

Barrel active-face area is 54.88-64.57% by layer; aligned sector-centre cracks remain. Custom masks give 69.47% endcap active-face area. At η=4, 68.89% of 360 one-degree-centred azimuth rays cross active silicon in at least one endcap layer; seams and guards leave blind directions. Native construction, IDs, mass and overlap checks plus sparse saved hits establish the isolated implementation; efficiencies and showers remain unvalidated.

[Barrel design and evidence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2776266570dda13386a16863e5b0e97432f27217/docs/design/DES-031-siw-barrel-prototype.md) · [Endcap design and evidence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/654b85a48abeb38735ad7fe0866c5d1082882df7/docs/design/DES-030-ecal-edge-sensors.md)

## 3 - ALLEGRO-style LAr ECAL prototype

Open component proposals: [PR #73](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/73) (LAr ECAL barrel and service interfaces prototype) and [PR #74](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/74) (LAr ECAL endcaps and layout prototype). The separate inner 3 T coil is retained; ALLEGRO’s outer-solenoid proxy is omitted.

| Element | Current prototype choice |
| --- | --- |
| Barrel sampling | 1,536 inclined periods, eleven compartments, two active gaps per electrode. Sampling radii 2.1728-2.5783 m; active half-length 3.910 m. Pb core 1.8 mm, total steel/glue 0.2/0.1 mm and 1.2 mm PCB; first core is passive LAr. |
| Turbine endcaps | Three wheels, 384/720/1,360 periods, 49° tilt, active r=410-2,790 mm and 450 mm depth. Inner Pb core 1.1 mm, total steel/glue 0.2/0.1 mm and 1.3 mm electrode. Radial/axial readout is virtual, distinct from source calibration subdivisions. |
| Supports / cold boards | Sixteen barrel H-rings and 5,888 wet board slots. Each endcap has three wheel support tubes, a 30 mm rear annulus (1.954 t/end) and 1,584 board slots. The unported rear annulus blocks direct signal/HV routes; passages and attachments need redesign. |
| Cryostat / cooling | Explicit warm/vacuum/cold wall proxies, 170 mm barrel rear bath and 250 mm endcap rear bath. N2 branches have 18 mm bore/20 mm OD; headers, seals, pressure/temperature and return-circuit qualification remain open. |

### Space and engineering consequences

The model has 2.286 million barrel cells and 601,600 per endcap. The Cartesian turbine taper differs from cylindrical-radius intent by up to 0.117 mm in the inner wheel. Physical mass includes bath displacement and cold service proxies. A 200 kW cooling allowance falls 58 kW short of the 258 kW adverse planning scenario, before complete static-heat qualification.

The 800 mm front gap budgets provisional cryogenic S-bends; this nODD routing choice is not an intrinsic LAr requirement. Native component checks and the ECAL-only combined audit do not qualify the tracker/coil/HCAL union. LAr remains uncovered at η=4; forward reservations contain no hardware. Barrel/endcap transition directions have partial depth, requiring later material/response design.

[Barrel/service design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/48e97256f8badd75c022a84ab1c4ff71977c56a2/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md) · [Endcap/forward design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/72d37ee9a56182e4ba974791a848a738c19cf092/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md)

## 4 - Budgets and review priorities

| Budget / boundary | Si-W candidate | LAr candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ECAL model mass: barrel / both ends / total | 299.003 / 98.949 / 397.952 t | 252.508 / 131.173 / 383.681 t |
| Principal material inventory | 198.595 t W alloy; 160.284 t Cu | 187.692 t Pb; 98.668 t LAr; 58.636 t Al |
| Barrel ECAL package bounds | Apothem 1.700-2.233 m; |z|≤3.920 m | Radius 2.100-2.830 m; |z|≤4.100 m |
| Endcap ECAL package bounds | |z|=3.950-4.483 m; outer apothem 2.223 m | |z|=4.900-5.860 m; outer radius 2.949 m |
| ECAL / HCAL routing allocations | 300 mm circular annulus; 400 mm rear egress break; 30 mm front seam is installation-only | 300 mm barrel radial; 181 mm beside endcap; 800/500 mm axial before/after endcap |
| Forward reservation | R=0.080-0.290 m; |z|=4.533-6.379 m; empty FCal | Empty EM collar and FCal; no active η=4 LAr coverage |
| HCAL outline extent | Outer apothem 4.096 m; |z|max=6.379 m | Outer apothem 4.626 m; |z|max=7.856 m |
| Outline max corner radius / full axial length | 4.176 m / 12.758 m | 4.717 m / 15.712 m |

ECAL masses are native-ledger sums with different passive/service hypotheses; shared tracker/solenoid, detailed HCAL and absent systems are excluded. Aluminium totals include walls, supports and boards. Masses do not rank performance. Compared with the service-amended Si-W layout, LAr HCAL outline volume is ×1.43; loads and magnetic effects remain unvalidated.

Shared tracker+Be inventory: 2.860 t (Be 2.036 kg); planning region r≤1.20 m, |z|≤3.60 m does not bound passive services. At η=0, separate examples are tracker 0.329-0.418 X0 and illustrative solenoid 1.402 X0 (1.00-2.10 scenarios). These are not a combined pre-ECAL map. Solenoid mass/support inventory remains unassigned. [Solenoid material assumptions](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/4e44d7c650ac0a2931f7fc1637b5b3f2dfbe4c95/docs/validation/DES-026/material-estimate.md).

### Bounded reviewer decisions

Review Si-W copper cooling, collector ports, balanced station wiring and custom-mask seams/process; review LAr vessel/support proxies, blocked service paths and cryogenic heat margin. Both have explicit external/forward space, with no installed FCal. Si-W merged lanes reserve 880×220 mm for a 166,698 mm² adverse load; its partial feed Cu/water estimates are 0.918/1.005 t, excluding other cables and supports. Routing, loads, shielding and beam-pipe continuation need separate design.

### Status and traceability

All four ECAL component PRs and service PR76 remain open in this 2026-10-14 snapshot. Dimensions/services are unsigned nODD choices; native budgets are model inferences. Recorded checks grant no engineering sign-off, installed field or shower/jet/particle-flow validation. This brief is a common review entry; the pinned component records remain authoritative.

[Frozen source and evidence catalogue](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/sources.json) · [Si-W layout inputs](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/layout001.json) · [LAr layout inputs](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/layout002.json)


## Superseded by the main-targeted calorimeter campaign

This ECAL reviewer overview contribution is retained in [replacement PR115](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/115). [Infrastructure PR116](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/116) preserves the original head, paired journals, exact canonical token ownership, public interactions and supersession map. Original branches and review history are retained.

Administrative closure grants no engineering approval. PR75’s outstanding human questions are carried into the replacement integration contract and follow-up tasks. Physical digitization, complete detector integration and qualification remain separate gates.

comments.body: Why does the ALLEGRO style barrel need a spacy gap between LAr Barrel and Endcap - and why is this not necessary for the Si-W prototype?

The **800 mm is a provisional nODD front-routing allocation**, rather than a demonstrated minimum for ALLEGRO or LAr calorimetry. The layouts currently use different service-exit strategies:

| | LAr LAYOUT-002 | Si-W LAYOUT-001 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ECAL barrel/endcap package gap | 800 mm for front cryogenic bends/access | 30 mm installation seam |
| Service route | Assumed front S-bend to the exterior backbone, then 500 mm rear HCAL break | Backbone outside both ECAL packages, then 400 mm rear HCAL break |
| Largest assumed jacket | 100 mm LAr utilities; 80 mm N2 | 50 mm water |

For LAr, the current calculation moves a pipe from R=2735.3 to 3029 mm. With a chosen bend radius of 4x100=400 mm, its two-arc S-bend occupies **739.4 mm**, including the 100 mm jacket and 20 mm clearance. This motivated the rounded 800 mm reservation. The cryostat end/front layers are already inside the package bounds; they do not independently justify the extra 800 mm. [Pinned service calculation](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/48e97256f8badd75c022a84ab1c4ff71977c56a2/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.py), [DES032](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/48e97256f8badd75c022a84ab1c4ff71977c56a2/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md#service-packing-and-amended-hcal-interface).

There is a missing premise: **the calculation uses the N2 exchanger radius for the 100 mm LAr utilities too**. Their actual headers, feedthrough origins and wall penetrations are undefined. The jacket sizes/bend rule are planning choices. The arithmetic sizes that assumed route; it cannot prove that the front gap is necessary or minimal.

Si-W has substantial service space as well. Its 300 mm exterior annulus continues outside both endcap and barrel corners; services exit radially through the **400 mm rear HCAL gap**. A chosen 50 mm water jacket needs 245 mm for one quarter-turn including clearance. Its 30 mm front seam is **not** the service-routing budget. Local cassette collectors/ports remain unresolved, so this topology is also an allocation rather than a qualified network. [DES034](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/0a26796518d690bf26934d2864d63ecad7582675/docs/design/DES-034-siw-service-envelopes.md#external-backbone-and-hcal-interfaces).

I have clarified both paragraphs in the overview and regenerated the matching four-page PDF. Proposed follow-up:

1. Define actual LAr header/feedthrough endpoints, jacket/bend/connector dimensions, supports and installation access; close the Si-W collector endpoints to the same standard.
2. Compare the present front S-bend with barrel-side outlets into the exterior annulus and rear egress. This is a plausible way to reduce the LAr front separation, subject to cryostat/route design.
3. Only then reduce/move the endcap and recheck containment, transition material/full-depth crossings and HCAL/collar/FCal interfaces. Keep 800 mm as the current reservation until an alternative is demonstrated.

[Retained explanation and bounded action proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/design/inputs/DES-032-transition-review.md). No geometry or performance claim has been changed by this reply.

1. In the ALLEGRO (Layout 002) geometry, what is the purpose of the (large) empty space between the magnet and the central ECAL? Is it related to services, cables, or the preshower (distance)?

2. Similarly, why are the ALLEGRO forward ECAL endcap "turbines" so far away from the central barrel along the z-axis? What is the service space between them needed for? Perhaps compare with the existing ALLEGRO references.

3. Why does the Si-W (Layout 001) proposal require much less service space, i.e., why is it more compact? Is this due to, for example, reduced cryogenic requirements because of the different calorimeter technology?

4. The cyan color (service space) and dashed gray (HCAL) are very similar, and I cannot actually see the dashing at all. The plots should be improved.

5. How are the materials and dimensions derived? Are they based on existing literature references and/or on optimization of some starting design? Describe the procedure.

6. What were the main physics performance criteria taken into account when deriving the designs? They look similar to previous HEP detectors, but give me the reasons.

7. Describe the procedure and simulations behind the mechanical engineering computations (flows, forces, masses, heat transfer, etc.), and/or provide a reference.

8. How is the 3D object geometry checked? Did you use an existing geometry processing package, or was something similar built on the fly, using geometry overlap/intersection algorithms such as AABB trees and/or ray tracing?

9. Give me an overall force/mass structure hierarchy and numbers, i.e., prove that the ECAL is not, for example, too heavy. Provide a reference for typical engineering design target values, i.e., what values (ranges) are actually feasible.

10. Give a systematic object structure of the 3D geometry that shows the distances to other objects, i.e., surface tolerances. That is, make it mathematically watertight that the necessary tolerances and empty spaces are satisfied and that all typical requirements (cabling, services, pipes, etc.) are taken into account.

11. Provide answers to the questions above for both designs, with an emphasis on the ECAL, but take into account the full detector as required.

# nODD ECAL layouts - reviewer overview

Si-W and ALLEGRO LAr candidates. Review entry, not a TDR.

Snapshot: 2026-10-14. [Four-page PDF](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/ecal-layout-review.pdf).

## 1 - Candidate layouts

Both candidates retain the documented tracker (45,646 sensitive planes) and the proposed inner solenoid (3 T central target; [PR #64](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/64), open). Its radial service reservation reaches 1.64 m; the computed vessel ends at r=1.559 m and |z|=3.85 m. These DRAFT prototypes have no complete-detector, installed-field or engineering acceptance.

![Si-W candidate R-Z view with tracker, conditional solenoid and HCAL outline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/figures/layout001-rz.png)

LAYOUT-001: Si-W ECAL, enlarged HCAL outline and empty service/FCal reservations. FCal and muon systems remain unbuilt.

![LAr candidate R-Z view with enlarged calorimeter and service allocations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/figures/layout002-rz.png)

LAYOUT-002: LAr ECAL, enlarged HCAL outline and empty service/forward reservations. Neither forward collar nor FCal is built.

## 2 - Si-W ECAL prototype

Open component proposals: [PR #71](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/71) (Si-W ECAL barrel prototype) and [PR #70](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/70) (Si-W ECAL endcap prototype). The same sampling and board stack is carried through sixteen barrel sectors and sixteen wedge carriers per endcap. [PR #76](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/76) adds service/forward envelopes under [DES034](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/0a26796518d690bf26934d2864d63ecad7582675/docs/design/DES-034-siw-service-envelopes.md).

| Element | Current prototype choice |
| --- | --- |
| Sampling / sensors | 48 layers; 1.9 mm tungsten alloy and 0.5 mm silicon. Standard 90 mm blanks have an 88 mm active window and 5.5 mm pad pitch; physical guards remain passive. |
| Barrel construction | Seven 1 m slabs plus two short end slabs per sector/layer. Alternating ±96 mm shifts move service joints through depth; 94 mm boards on a 96 mm pitch retain real gaps. |
| Endcap packing | 76 squares plus 36 custom edge sensors per wedge/layer; 29 mask profiles. The 100 mm aperture apothem, 30 mm inner support and 120 mm outer service bay are unsigned allocations. |
| Support / cooling | Aluminium skins and frames, explicit PCB/ASIC/thermal contacts; a 3 mm copper plate with 2 mm-OD Ti/water runs. External collectors/ports remain absent; PR76 reserves an outer backbone and HCAL rear egress. |

### Material and service drivers

Recorded model masses are 299.003 t for the barrel and 98.949 t for both endcaps. Copper contributes 119.693/40.591 t, dominated by the cooling plates. Continuous heat hypotheses give 188.40/71.05 kW; the summed ideal water flow is 12.414 kg/s for a 5 K rise. These are inventory/power calculations, not thermal or hydraulic qualification. A 300 mm annulus and 400 mm rear break reserve cable/water exits; local cassette ports and support loads remain open. The 30 mm front seam is installation-only; services are allocated outside the endcap.

### Coverage and evidence limits

Barrel active-face area is 54.88-64.57% by layer; aligned sector-centre cracks remain. Custom masks give 69.47% endcap active-face area. At η=4, 68.89% of 360 one-degree-centred azimuth rays cross active silicon in at least one endcap layer; seams and guards leave blind directions. Native construction, IDs, mass and overlap checks plus sparse saved hits establish the isolated implementation; efficiencies and showers remain unvalidated.

[Barrel design and evidence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2776266570dda13386a16863e5b0e97432f27217/docs/design/DES-031-siw-barrel-prototype.md) · [Endcap design and evidence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/654b85a48abeb38735ad7fe0866c5d1082882df7/docs/design/DES-030-ecal-edge-sensors.md)

## 3 - ALLEGRO-style LAr ECAL prototype

Open component proposals: [PR #73](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/73) (LAr ECAL barrel and service interfaces prototype) and [PR #74](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/74) (LAr ECAL endcaps and layout prototype). The separate inner 3 T coil is retained; ALLEGRO’s outer-solenoid proxy is omitted.

| Element | Current prototype choice |
| --- | --- |
| Barrel sampling | 1,536 inclined periods, eleven compartments, two active gaps per electrode. Sampling radii 2.1728-2.5783 m; active half-length 3.910 m. Pb core 1.8 mm, total steel/glue 0.2/0.1 mm and 1.2 mm PCB; first core is passive LAr. |
| Turbine endcaps | Three wheels, 384/720/1,360 periods, 49° tilt, active r=410-2,790 mm and 450 mm depth. Inner Pb core 1.1 mm, total steel/glue 0.2/0.1 mm and 1.3 mm electrode. Radial/axial readout is virtual, distinct from source calibration subdivisions. |
| Supports / cold boards | Sixteen barrel H-rings and 5,888 wet board slots. Each endcap has three wheel support tubes, a 30 mm rear annulus (1.954 t/end) and 1,584 board slots. The unported rear annulus blocks direct signal/HV routes; passages and attachments need redesign. |
| Cryostat / cooling | Explicit warm/vacuum/cold wall proxies, 170 mm barrel rear bath and 250 mm endcap rear bath. N2 branches have 18 mm bore/20 mm OD; headers, seals, pressure/temperature and return-circuit qualification remain open. |

### Space and engineering consequences

The model has 2.286 million barrel cells and 601,600 per endcap. The Cartesian turbine taper differs from cylindrical-radius intent by up to 0.117 mm in the inner wheel. Physical mass includes bath displacement and cold service proxies. A 200 kW cooling allowance falls 58 kW short of the 258 kW adverse planning scenario, before complete static-heat qualification.

The 800 mm front gap budgets provisional cryogenic S-bends; this nODD routing choice is not an intrinsic LAr requirement. Native component checks and the ECAL-only combined audit do not qualify the tracker/coil/HCAL union. LAr remains uncovered at η=4; forward reservations contain no hardware. Barrel/endcap transition directions have partial depth, requiring later material/response design.

[Barrel/service design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/48e97256f8badd75c022a84ab1c4ff71977c56a2/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md) · [Endcap/forward design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/72d37ee9a56182e4ba974791a848a738c19cf092/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md)

## 4 - Budgets and review priorities

| Budget / boundary | Si-W candidate | LAr candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ECAL model mass: barrel / both ends / total | 299.003 / 98.949 / 397.952 t | 252.508 / 131.173 / 383.681 t |
| Principal material inventory | 198.595 t W alloy; 160.284 t Cu | 187.692 t Pb; 98.668 t LAr; 58.636 t Al |
| Barrel ECAL package bounds | Apothem 1.700-2.233 m; |z|≤3.920 m | Radius 2.100-2.830 m; |z|≤4.100 m |
| Endcap ECAL package bounds | |z|=3.950-4.483 m; outer apothem 2.223 m | |z|=4.900-5.860 m; outer radius 2.949 m |
| ECAL / HCAL routing allocations | 300 mm circular annulus; 400 mm rear egress break; 30 mm front seam is installation-only | 300 mm barrel radial; 181 mm beside endcap; 800/500 mm axial before/after endcap |
| Forward reservation | R=0.080-0.290 m; |z|=4.533-6.379 m; empty FCal | Empty EM collar and FCal; no active η=4 LAr coverage |
| HCAL outline extent | Outer apothem 4.096 m; |z|max=6.379 m | Outer apothem 4.626 m; |z|max=7.856 m |
| Outline max corner radius / full axial length | 4.176 m / 12.758 m | 4.717 m / 15.712 m |

ECAL masses are native-ledger sums with different passive/service hypotheses; shared tracker/solenoid, detailed HCAL and absent systems are excluded. Aluminium totals include walls, supports and boards. Masses do not rank performance. Compared with the service-amended Si-W layout, LAr HCAL outline volume is ×1.43; loads and magnetic effects remain unvalidated.

Shared tracker+Be inventory: 2.860 t (Be 2.036 kg); planning region r≤1.20 m, |z|≤3.60 m does not bound passive services. At η=0, separate examples are tracker 0.329-0.418 X0 and illustrative solenoid 1.402 X0 (1.00-2.10 scenarios). These are not a combined pre-ECAL map. Solenoid mass/support inventory remains unassigned. [Solenoid material assumptions](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/4e44d7c650ac0a2931f7fc1637b5b3f2dfbe4c95/docs/validation/DES-026/material-estimate.md).

### Bounded reviewer decisions

Review Si-W copper cooling, collector ports, balanced station wiring and custom-mask seams/process; review LAr vessel/support proxies, blocked service paths and cryogenic heat margin. Both have explicit external/forward space, with no installed FCal. Si-W merged lanes reserve 880×220 mm for a 166,698 mm² adverse load; its partial feed Cu/water estimates are 0.918/1.005 t, excluding other cables and supports. Routing, loads, shielding and beam-pipe continuation need separate design.

### Status and traceability

All four ECAL component PRs and service PR76 remain open in this 2026-10-14 snapshot. Dimensions/services are unsigned nODD choices; native budgets are model inferences. Recorded checks grant no engineering sign-off, installed field or shower/jet/particle-flow validation. This brief is a common review entry; the pinned component records remain authoritative.

[Frozen source and evidence catalogue](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/sources.json) · [Si-W layout inputs](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/layout001.json) · [LAr layout inputs](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-layout-review-entry/docs/layouts/review/layout002.json)


## Superseded by the main-targeted calorimeter campaign

This ECAL reviewer overview contribution is retained in [replacement PR115](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/115). [Infrastructure PR116](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/116) preserves the original head, paired journals, exact canonical token ownership, public interactions and supersession map. Original branches and review history are retained.

Administrative closure grants no engineering approval. PR75’s outstanding human questions are carried into the replacement integration contract and follow-up tasks. Physical digitization, complete detector integration and qualification remain separate gates.
Why does the ALLEGRO style barrel need a spacy gap between LAr Barrel and Endcap - and why is this not necessary for the Si-W prototype?

The **800 mm is a provisional nODD front-routing allocation**, rather than a demonstrated minimum for ALLEGRO or LAr calorimetry. The layouts currently use different service-exit strategies:

| | LAr LAYOUT-002 | Si-W LAYOUT-001 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ECAL barrel/endcap package gap | 800 mm for front cryogenic bends/access | 30 mm installation seam |

The proposed outer backbone and rear HCAL break are credible **space allocations** while preserving PR70/71 ECAL packages and placements. Physical cassette collectors and penetrations remain unresolved, as they do for the LAr prototype.

**Source-count reconciliation**

The native `interface` role counts include passive shared PCBs:

- Barrel: **22,560 = 15,648 powered interface chips + 6,912 shared PCBs**. There is one PCB per slab/layer/sector: 9×48×16.
- Both endcaps: **6,144 = 4,608 powered interface chips + 1,536 shared PCBs**. Each wedge/layer has one PCB and three interface chips.

Thus 15,648 barrel interfaces and 2,304 per endcap govern the recorded interface-power hypothesis and external link allocation. Using the larger native role counts as independently powered units would double-count passive PCBs.

Exact primary locators:

- PR71 revision `2776266570dda13386a16863e5b0e97432f27217`, `tools/calorimeter_hardware/barrel_export.py:60–63`; `barrel_layout.py:58–73`; `docs/validation/DES-031/native.json`, `physical_counts`.

**External station and packing proposal**

These are **unsigned NODD DESIGN CHOICES**, following the existing LAr allocation conventions rather than selected Si-W cable hardware:

| Quantity | Barrel | Each endcap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Stations | 32: 16 sectors × 2 ends | 16: one per wedge |
| Powered interfaces/station, balanced average | 489 | 144 |
| 2.5 mm data-pair cables/station | 1,956 | 576 |
| 2 mm fibres/station | 1,956 | 576 |
| 3 mm HV cables/station | 12 | 20 |
| Power/ground/control cables/station | 4×12 / 2×8 / 4×3 mm | Same |
| Supply/return water jackets/station | 2×50 mm OD | Same |
| Nominal packed area, 40% fill | 50,849 mm² | 23,216 mm² |
| Adverse area: double data/fibres, 30% fill | 120,286 mm² | 46,412 mm² |

Four data pairs and four fibres per interface are deliberately conservative routing hypotheses, not a qualified bandwidth architecture. The balanced barrel station assignment and local collector graph are not yet demonstrated.

A **700×150 mm** lane fits nominal loads but fails the barrel adverse scenario. A **900×150 mm** lane fits each subsystem separately. At each rear junction the combined barrel/endcap nominal area is **74,065 mm²**, and adverse area **166,698 mm²**. Reserve a **900×220 mm junction envelope**, centred at **R=2.430 m**, to contain both:

- inner radial face: 2.320 m;
- far corner: √(2.540²+0.450²) = **2.5796 m**;
- maximum angular extent: atan(0.450/2.320) = **10.98°**, below the 11.25° half-sector;
- capacity: **198,000 mm²**, with approximately 20 mm clearance to each circular backbone boundary.

This checks footprint containment, not installed packing, connector access or a complete bend network.

Using the LAr-style 20 m/barrel-station and 12 m/endcap-station route hypotheses gives:

| Cable length | Barrel | Each endcap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Data pairs / fibres | 1,251.840 / 1,251.840 km | 110.592 / 110.592 km |
| HV | 7.680 km | 3.840 km |
| Power / ground / control | 2.560 / 1.280 / 2.560 km | 0.768 / 0.384 / 0.768 km |
| Water jackets, supply + return | 1.280 km | 0.384 km |

These large Si-W link lengths expose the cost of exporting every existing interface without further aggregation. Optical-only backbones or local multiplexing are alternatives requiring electronics, heat and bandwidth assessment. Retain ±50% route-length uncertainty; these sums include routes outside the detector handoff and are not installed mass.

**Cooling and electrical input**

Reproducing the pinned formulas gives:

- Barrel heat: **188.401475 kW**.
- Each endcap: **35.525470 kW**.
- Total: **259.452415 kW**.
- Ideal water at 4,180 J/(kg·K), ΔT=5 K: **12.413991 kg/s**.
- Per station: barrel **0.281701 kg/s**, endcap **0.106236 kg/s**.

A chosen **20 mm water bore inside the 50 mm external jacket** gives nominal bulk velocities of **0.897 / 0.338 m/s**. A 1.5× load scenario requires **18.621 kg/s total**, before hydraulic/thermal qualification.

The source heat formula already includes 90%-efficient conversion; do **not** divide it by 0.9 again. A new 48 V upstream feed hypothesis gives **122.66 / 46.26 A per barrel/endcap station**. With two parallel 25 mm² Cu conductors per polarity, a 40 m supply-plus-return loop and ρ=1.72×10⁻⁸ Ωm:

- nominal drops: **1.688 / 0.636 V**;
- nominal external losses: **207.0 / 29.4 W per station**;
- 1.5× load drops: **2.532 / 0.955 V**;
- aggregate nominal external cable loss: **7.57 kW**, additional to the recorded local ECAL heat.

Ampacity, converter placement, voltage drop at temperature and removal of external cable heat are unqualified.

There are **51,552 local coolant runs and 103,104 endpoints** across the ECAL. Hierarchical collectors are essential. The proposed backbone does not connect those endpoints automatically.

| Allocation | Proposed value |
|---|---:|
| Circular service backbone | R=2.300–2.600 m |
| HCAL barrel inner / outer apothems | 2.600 / 4.0959 m |
| HCAL barrel half-length | 4.4832 m |

A simple non-overlapping alternative is an **empty FCal reservation**:

- R=0.080–0.290 m;
- |z|=4.5332–6.3791 m;
- 50 mm behind ECAL;
- 10 mm inside HCAL's minimum circular aperture, set by its 0.300 m inner apothem.

- rear collar: R=0.080–0.450 m, |z|4.5332–4.8332 m;
- narrow FCal: R=0.080–0.290 m, |z|4.8332–6.3791 m.

The **800 mm LAr gap is a selected nODD routing allowance, not an intrinsic requirement of ALLEGRO or LAr calorimetry**. The comparison is between different service topologies:

| | LAr LAYOUT-002 | Si-W LAYOUT-001 |
|---|---|---|
| Barrel/endcap package gap | 800 mm, reserved for front service bends/access | 30 mm, installation seam only |
| Exterior route | R≈3.029 m, outside endcap cryostat | Circular R=2.300–2.600 m backbone |

| Largest assumed pipe jacket | 100 mm LAr utilities; 80 mm N₂ | 50 mm water |
| Selected bend calculation | Front two-arc S-bend; rear quarter-turn | Rear quarter-turn |
| Physical connection status | Ports, seals, headers and routes unengineered | Cassette collectors/ports and routes unengineered |

**The recorded LAr arithmetic is correct for its assumptions.** `services.py:46–58` uses a radial shift of **3029−2735.3=293.7 mm**, with chosen bend radius **4×100=400 mm**. Two opposite arcs give:

- axial centreline span: **619.403 mm**;
- plus 20 mm clearance and 100 mm OD: **739.403 mm**;
- 800 mm allocation leaves **60.597 mm** nominal margin;
- rear 90° turn: 400+50+20 = **470 mm**, within the 500 mm rear break.

For the 80 mm jacket, the corresponding front envelope is **638.216 mm**.

**The missing premise is the utility starting point.** The code applies the **barrel N₂ exchanger radius, 2735.3 mm, to both N₂ and 100 mm LAr utilities**. No utility-specific feedthrough origin, wall penetration or header route establishes that common origin. The 4×OD bend rule, jacket diameters and access allowance are also nODD choices, not qualified vendor constraints. Thus the calculation sizes a chosen path; it does not prove that every service must use that path or that 800 mm is the minimum feasible transition.

Cryogenic walls and access do add space beyond warm mechanical Si-W packaging, but they are already included in the LAr package bounds. The barrel active half-length is **3.910 m**, its warm end **4.100 m**; the endcap warm front is **4.900 m**, sampling front **5.010 m**. The separate **800 mm external gap excludes the 190 mm barrel-end and 110 mm endcap-front passive allocations**. These are prototype proxies, not an engineered pressure-vessel requirement.

Practical follow-ups:

1. **Correct the comparison wording now.** Say “chosen front routing allocation” for LAr and “installation-only seam, with exterior/rear routing” for Si-W. DES032’s comparison with “SiW’s small installation gaps” predates DES034 and should not imply that Si-W services fit into 30 mm.
2. **Define real interface endpoints before shrinking the gap.** Name each utility’s cold header, warm feedthrough location, pipe OD/bend constraints, seals, removable connection and support/access envelope. The N₂ exchanger radius cannot substitute for all origins.
3. **Compare two LAr routes with the same geometric checks used for Si-W.** Retain the current front S-bend as a control; investigate radial outlets into the exterior annulus, with axial routing beside the endcap and rear egress through the existing 500 mm break. This might reduce front separation, but requires cryostat/header redesign and a swept-volume check.
4. **Use intermediate reductions only as explicit studies.** For illustration, a 100 mm jacket beginning at R=2.900 m rather than 2.7353 m would need approximately **555.6 mm** for the same S-bend convention to R=3.029 m.
